chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Sahl ibn al-Adami, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn Marid, that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: (The Most Compassionate is firm on the Empyrean)
He (peace be upon him) replied: He is equal to everything, so there is no thing that is closer to Him than another thing.

key_terms.اسْتَوَى: He established Himself / He is firm / He is equal
key_terms.الرَّحْمَنُ: The Most Compassionate, a divine name
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: The Throne, often symbolizing divine authority or the cosmos

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when Allah is described as being 'firm on the Throne'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the attribute of *istiwa* (establishment) on the Throne not as physical movement or sitting, but as a state of absolute equality in proximity to all creation, thereby negating literal spatial dimensions (*jismaniyyah*). This interpretation aligns with the Shia theological principle of *tanzih* (divine transcendence), distinguishing between the Throne as a sign of authority rather than a physical location. It serves as a foundational counter to anthropomorphic views, emphasizing that Allah’s presence is not confined by distance or direction.
